title: Noor and the Playlist
premise: Oscar Delacroix, the quiet statistician who keeps everyone else's secrets in spreadsheets, has one real friend: Noor Haddad, who curates a shared playlist that says everything neither of them can. When Noor vanishes, leaving only a keyring and a final uploaded track, Oscar decodes the song order as a map pointing to the town's founding tradition — the Harvest Lantern Walk — and discovers the 'rigged game' Noor uncovered: the festival committee has been falsifying its history to erase the immigrant families, including Noor's, who actually built it. Following the playlist through archives, attics, and the flooded old mill, Oscar gathers a found family of outsiders to restore the true record before the committee buries it at this year's Walk. In the climax, Oscar publicly reads the recovered ledger as the lanterns rise, and Noor — who staged the disappearance to force the town to listen — steps out of the crowd; the tradition survives, but remade honestly, with Noor's family name restored to its founder's plaque.
about_author: Yara Ishikawa is a former high school debate coach who grew up between a Louisiana bayou town and her grandmother's house in Osaka, and writes about kids who translate themselves for everyone else. She lives with two cats named after failed space missions and still makes playlists for people she loves.

chapters.title: Track One
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Establishes Oscar's invisible-kid routine: stats binder, shut locker, one lunch table shared with Noor, whose playlists are their only language. The chapter ends with Noor not showing up to sixth period, and a text from an unknown number: just a song title. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Keys on the Bench
chapters.summary: Oscar finds Noor's keyring taped under their usual bench — three unlabeled keys and a USB drive. Principal Voss dismisses the disappearance as runaway behavior. Oscar's mother urges them to stay out of it. Beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Shuffle Is a Lie
chapters.summary: Oscar realizes the USB holds a 22-track playlist in deliberate order, each song titled after a location or date. First stop: the county archive basement, where they meet Priya, a sharp-tongued volunteer archivist. Beat: the first spark of alliance.

chapters.title: What the Plaque Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The founder's plaque credits only the Beaumont family, but archive ledgers show four families signed the original mill charter — including Haddad. Oscar feels the first vertigo of a town built on an edited story. Beat: betrayal by history itself.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: The second key opens a school locker Noor secretly rented, stuffed with committee meeting notes and a photo of the mill before it 'burned.' Oscar recruits Theo, Noor's estranged cousin, who knows the tunnels under the old mill. Beat: found family begins assembling.

chapters.title: The Rigged Score
chapters.summary: Oscar runs the numbers on the festival's scholarship fund and proves money is being siphoned through the Heritage Committee — the same fund Noor was denied. POV shifts briefly to Priya finding a doctored minute book. Beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: Interlude: What Noor Left Playing
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, told through unsent voice memos recorded before disappearing. Reveals Noor discovered the erasure while researching a school project and decided to make the town look for what it buried. Beat: reframing everything — Noor chose this.

chapters.title: Key Three
chapters.summary: The third key fits a storage unit holding the original 1911 charter and a lantern from the first Walk, engraved with four names. Committee member Dale Beaumont confronts them, all charm and threat. Beat: the enemy shows its face.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Oscar's mother finds the charter in Oscar's room; a raw fight about survival, visibility, and why Oscar always hides. Oscar admits staying invisible never protected anyone. Beat: lowest personal point, turning toward courage.

chapters.title: The Mill Tunnels
chapters.summary: Theo leads Oscar and Priya into the flooded mill passages following the playlist's midpoint tracks. They find Noor's camp: notes, food wrappers weeks old, and a wall mapping every erased family. But no Noor. Beat: dread deepens — where is she really?

chapters.title: Voss Knows
chapters.summary: Principal Voss catches them returning and, instead of punishing them, quietly returns a confiscated box of Noor's things — revealing Voss once tried to expose the committee herself and was broken by it. Beat: unexpected ally, generational regret.

chapters.title: Track Seventeen
chapters.summary: Decoding the seventeenth song leads to the cemetery and the unmarked grave of Amal Haddad, the true co-founder. Priya identifies the fourth family too: hers. The erasure was never random — it was targeted. Beat: grief fusing into purpose.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Dale Beaumont offers Oscar a full-ride scholarship and silence, exploiting the family's precarity. Oscar almost takes it. A late-night call with Theo and Priya pulls them back. Beat: temptation and refusal — identity over safety.

chapters.title: Missing Poster Season
chapters.summary: Town splits as search volunteers clash with committee loyalists; someone trashes the archive room. Oscar realizes the committee isn't hiding Noor — they're terrified of what she'll surface next. Beat: stakes widen from personal to civic.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Wall
chapters.summary: Following the final tracks' timestamps, Oscar pries open the mill's sealed office and finds the complete payroll ledger proving four founding families — plus evidence the fire that 'destroyed' the records was set deliberately. Beat: the weapon is finally in hand.

chapters.title: Countdown to the Walk
chapters.summary: Three days to the Lantern Walk; the committee moves to demolish the mill early. The group plans to read the ledger aloud during the ceremony when every ear in town is listening. Beat: tension coiling toward the climax.

chapters.title: Demolition Day
chapters.summary: Oscar chains themself to the mill gate in a desperate stall while Priya livestreams and Theo fetches the state preservation officer. Dale calls Oscar's bluff; then the crowd of students arrives. Beat: Oscar stops being invisible — publicly, irreversibly.

chapters.title: The Lantern Walk
chapters.summary: Climax. As lanterns rise, Oscar takes the stage and reads the charter names; Voss corroborates; the crowd turns. Dale accuses them of staging everything — and then Noor walks out of the crowd, alive, holding the last lantern. Beat: shock, fury, relief colliding.

chapters.title: Why You Let Us Look
chapters.summary: Noor explains: she couldn't be heard as herself, so she made the town search — made them find the truth with their own hands. Oscar rages, then understands. Beat: the cost of the plan admitted, friendship tested and mended.

chapters.title: Amendments
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the committee resigns, the scholarship is audited, and the council votes to recast the plaque with all four names. Noor faces consequences for the hoax and accepts them. Beat: justice without fantasy — repair is work.

chapters.title: B-Sides
chapters.summary: Quiet epilogue-adjacent chapter: Oscar, Noor, Priya, and Theo repaint the mill together, trading stories; Oscar starts a new playlist called 'Found.' Beat: tenderness, the found family settled into itself.

chapters.title: Track Twenty-Two
chapters.summary: Final scene at the relit Lantern Walk, now honoring the true founders. Noor adds a new song to their shared playlist; Oscar presses play as the lanterns rise. Last line lands on inheritance chosen, not assigned. Beat: hopeful, earned resolution.
